notes.title: Patch 1.0.9 Release
notes.content:
[b]Patch 1.0.9[/b] takes your feedback on the player rig causing issues with motion sickness into account and has been our primary focus.

We've adjusted the player rig to prevent the world pushing the player back when they push against static objects.

The Scallywag Crew continue to work on improving Taskmaster VR, so stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Patch 1.0.8b Release
notes.content:
[h2]Patch 1.0.8b Release![/h2]


[b]Happy New Year![/b]
We hope you had a great festive season! Just a short note from us to let you all know that Patch 1.0.8b will be releasing today, which will revert our jolly Taskmaster and his impish assistant back to their classic, black-jacketed selves. This patch also contains some small bug fixes, and a much requested quality of life update!

[h3]CHRISTMAS IS CANCELLED[/h3]
[list]
[*] The Winter Holiday event is ending, and everything in the Taskmaster House is returning to normal. It was fun while it lasted!
[/list]

[h3]NEW FEATURE: IMPROVED DOORS[/h3]
[list]
[*] When using continuous locomotion, doors will now stay open after you open them, and will automatically close when you are a set distance away. This should provide fewer instances of players getting stuck in doors, and moving around the house should be a smoother experience.
[*] When using teleport locomotion, doors will now open automatically when they intersect with the teleport tool. This is an important accessibility change that means Teleport players will be able to move through the Taskmaster house much quicker.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/5e4980da32178356a9ff2e63ebe64bf8bf65ad7b.gif[/img]

[h3]MISC[/h3]
[list]
[*]A number of minor bug fixes, including one on Dietary Intervention that could rarely cause player positions to reset at random.
[/list]

Let us know how the new doors feel for you, and what we can do to improve them further! See you soon!

notes.title: The Winter Holiday update has arrived!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/cec42803b33fc1d2904d963079b8c897875f88f5.png[/img]

Scallywag Arcade are excited to share the news that patch 1.0.8 is releasing for Taskmaster VR! There’s been a jolly overhaul to the Taskmaster house, and Greg and Alex have gotten into the festive spirit themselves! Plus, a whole new feature and way to play the game - introducing Challenges!

[list]
[*] The holiday update is here! Lots of seasonal goodies and new toys to play with will transform Series Play into a festive, bell-jingling treat.
[*] Challenges are now available! Explore the Taskmaster house and solve plenty of playful puzzles to earn presents from the Taskmaster!
[*] Plenty of bug fixes and minor quality of life changes.
[*] Some tweaks and changes to get ready for the new year, and the next update - and it's going to be a big one…
[/list]

We’d like to thank every single player who has come with us on our Taskmaster VR journey this year - we can’t wait to Share what’s next with you!


[h2]Game-wide Updates[/h2]
[h3]Winter Holiday Seasonal Event[/h3]
[list]
[*] We all had a great time getting spooky with Alex and his Taskmonster - but now we’re feeling a little bit jollier - Series Play mode is now fully playable with the Winter Theme, with lots of new objects and tools to play with!
[*] We’ve added a bunch of new easter  eggs and secrets to discover throughout the house, Alex and his elves have been busy! Throw snowballs, toss some logs on the fire - you can even build a snowman!
[*] Seasonally appropriate new outfits for Alex and Greg.
[*] The Winter Holiday is a limited time event, and will be ending in January - don’t miss out!
[/list]

[h3]Challenges are Here![/h3]
[list]
[*] Explore the taskmaster house in a whole new way! The Challenges board will grant access to special, alternative versions of the taskmaster house, each with their own unique rubber duck trophy to unlock.
[*] Optional clues provide a difficulty adjustment if things are getting ever so slightly too cryptic.
[*] Complete every challenge and unlock a brand new trophy for your cabinet!
[*] Challenges are playful, short form bites of Taskmaster goodness, and we’re really keen to get player feedback - where could we take these next?
[/list]

[h3]The Corkboard Quarters[/h3]
[list]
[*] The corkboard quarters have had a minor layout change to accommodate challenges and some other smaller features.
[*] A new television has been added to the space, and will be used to communicate the latest news, competitions and opportunities that may not be directly related to gameplay.
[*] Mini-Tasks have been removed, in preparation for Update 1.1 in 2025.
[*] We’re aware the Corkboard Quarters are starting to feel a little cramped, and some changes have been made in preparation for a refresh next year.
[/list]

[h3]Achievements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Removed the Up For More Tasks? Achievement, in preparation for update 1.1 in 2025.
[/list]

[h3]Other Stuff[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixes to a number of materials that were not displaying as intended.
[*] Adjusted LOD bias and distances to improve performance and visuals when outside.
[*] Lots of minor bug fixes and performance optimisations.
[/list]

notes.title: Spooky Season Event - It’s Halloween!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/0fb86b85b121964bb69ff0d0f6bae2839e881bb8.png[/img]

Patch 1.0.7 is releasing for Taskmaster VR! This patch primarily releases a spooky, seasonal skin for the game, filled with lots of little tricks and treats! Some of the highlights include -
[list]
[*] The Spooky Update! OOoooOOOh!
[*] Contextual Scoreboard visuals! 
[*] “Ghost Hands” are now optional!
[*] Bug fixes and minor task balance changes!
[/list]
We have plenty more improvements to make, and we encourage further feedback as we move into our next phase of development support - thank you!

[h2]Game-wide Updates  [/h2]
[h3]Spooky Season Event - It’s Halloween![/h3]
[list]
[*] Summer is officially over, and the house theme has been overhauled for spooky season!
[*] The whole game is playable in Spooky Mode - with tons of new tools and objects to play with, some of which have some….unnatural…properties!
[*] Lots of new easter eggs (halloween eggs?) and secrets to discover - can you find all the ducks that Alex and his coven have hidden around the house?
[*] Seasonally appropriate outfits for the Taskmaster and his Assistant - Trick or Treat!
[*] Spooky new music!
[*] Spooky Season is a limited time event, so don’t miss out!
[/list]
[h3]General Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] “Ghost Hands” are now an optional feature that can be turned off in the Journal - Player hands in Taskmaster are physics objects in the world, and for many players, having a separate indicator of your controller location is a necessary accessibility consideration. However, we realise that many of our players, including streamers, want a more visually immersive experience, so we have updated this feature to be optional.
[*] Ghost Hands will remain on by default, because it is halloween. 
[*] Stickers in the Journal that were missing animations will now animate correctly.
[*] An issue where player hands could sometimes duplicate themselves has been solved.
[*] Additional code cleanup and optimisation has been performed across the game, which should result in even fewer framerate spikes or slowdown periods.
[/list]

[h2]Task-Specific Updates[/h2]
[h3]Chimp’s First Day at the Deli Shop[/h3]
[list]
[*] An image of your delicious sandwich will now be displayed on the scoreboard during the scoring sequence, providing context to Greg’s comments. Mmm, delicious!
[/list]
[h3]Artistic Flatmate[/h3]
[list]
[*] An image of your sticky note artwork will now be displayed next to the original painting during scoreboard, providing better context to Greg’s comments and showing players just how rubbish they are at modern art.
[/list]
[h3]Who Needs Smartphones?[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause dialogue to play extremely slowly during this task, as well as lowering framerate.
[/list]
[h3]Just Feed The Dog Some Watermelon[/h3]
[list]
[*] The dog food should no longer defy gravity if you are holding the dog bowl. Can you believe how wild some of these patch notes are? Imagine having to write that sentence with a straight face.
[/list]

[h2]OTHER STUFF![/h2]
[h3]Known Issues[/h3]
As with any major update, we are aware of some lingering issues as a result of our changes that are being worked on for an upcoming patch/hotfix. In the interests of transparency, we have documented these below.

[list]
[*] Very rarely, the player's hands can desync from the controllers during scoring. We are investigating the cause, but this should not block gameplay progression.
[*] Alex’s facial animation will sometimes not play as he is talking. This does not affect progression and is under investigation.
[*] Certain plate colliders can occasionally have physics issues. We are investigating the cause.
[*] Moving through doors when using teleport movement mechanics is slightly more labour intensive than intended - we are working on an update to the teleport mechanic to address this.
[*] ‘Strike!’ achievement has been temporarily disabled, while we investigate a possible issue that can occur when unlocking this achievement.
[/list]

notes.title: Taskmaster VR Patch 1.0.6 - out now!
notes.content:
[h1]Patch Notes - v1.0.6 - Steam[/h1]
[h2]22.08.2024[/h2]

Scallywag Arcade are excited to share the news that patch 1.0.6 is releasing for Taskmaster VR! This patch primarily focuses on addressing a number of remaining issues identified by our community, as well as helping prepare for upcoming game updates. Some of the highlights of this patch include;

[list]
[*] Fixes to a number of Steam achievements that were not firing correctly.
[*] The addition of a trophy cabinet!
[*] Improved and optimised graphics.
[*] Bug fixes and minor task balance changes.
[*] And more!
[/list]

We have plenty more improvements to make, and we encourage further feedback as we move into our next phase of development support - thank you!

[h2]Game-wide Updates[/h2]  
[h3]New Feature - The Trophy Cabinet[/h3]
[list]
[*] A trophy cabinet has been added to the hub!
[*] Collect and display up to four unique trophies, based on your final score in Series Play.
[/list]
[h3]Achievements[/h3]
[list]
[*] ‘Not Quite Gold’ should now unlock properly on Steam.
[*] ‘A Smashing Time’ should now unlock properly on Steam.
[*] ‘A Treat For The Taskmaster’ should now unlock properly on Steam.
[*] ‘Taskmaster and Commander’ and ‘Up For More Tasks?’ have been temporarily removed pending future updates to Creative Mode. Watch this space!
[/list]
[h3]Audio[/h3]
[list]
[*] New dialogue lines have been added for Greg and Alex throughout the game.
[*] Removed even more awkward silences between Greg and Alex, improving their relationship.
[*] Greg will now correctly muse on what we have learnt today at the end of Episode 1.
[*] New ambient SFX in the Dome. One for the real domeheads out there.
[*] Improved collision sound effects on knives, for the worrying amount of you trying to cut everything. This is a family show!
[*] New unique SFX for a large number of items, including but not limited to the Fish Slice, Lava Lamp, Boom Box and First Aid Kit.
[*] Lots of other minor SFX improvements, throughout various areas and menus of the game.
[/list]
[h3]GUI[/h3]
[list]
[*] Optimisation and compression of 2D assets resulting in improved visual clarity and performance gains. I don’t have a joke for this one.
[/list]

[h2]OTHER STUFF![/h2]
[h3]Known Issues[/h3]
As with any major update, we are aware of some lingering issues as a result of our changes that are being worked on for an upcoming patch/hotfix. In the interests of transparency, we have documented these below.
[list]
[*] Very rarely, the player's hands can desync from the controllers during scoring. We are investigating the cause, but this should not block gameplay progression.
[*] Alex’s facial animation will sometimes not play as he is talking. This does not affect progression and is under investigation.
[*] Certain plate colliders can occasionally have physics issues. We are investigating the cause.
[*] Moving through doors when using teleport movement mechanics is slightly more labour intensive than intended - we are working on an update to the teleport mechanic to address this in the next update.
[*] ‘Strike!’ achievement has been temporarily disabled, while we investigate a possible issue that can occur when unlocking this achievement.
[/list]

notes.title: Taskmaster VR Patch 1.0.5 - out now!
notes.content:
[h1]Patch Notes - v1.0.5 - Steam[/h1]
[h2]25.07.2024[/h2]

Scallywag Arcade are excited to share the news that patch 1.0.5 is releasing for Taskmaster VR! This first patch primarily focuses on addressing the display issues reported by some of our players, but also brings bug fixes, balance changes, and quality of life improvements to the table.

[list]
[*] A major overhaul of render pipelines, resulting in significant improvements to performance across all areas of the game.
[*] Initial adjustments to in-game physics stability.
[*] Balance passes across all tasks, improving how tasks are scored by Greg, alongside a number of mechanical changes to improve the player experience.
[*] Improved and optimised graphical assets to address issues some players were having with “blurry” GUI.
[*] And much more!
[/list]

We’re not finished yet, but we believe this patch will help those affected by the reported issues play the game as intended. We have plenty more improvements to make, and we encourage further feedback as we move into our next phase of development support - thank you!

[h2]Game-wide Updates[/h2]  
[h3]Performance & Display[/h3]
[list]
[*] Optimised occlusion settings to improve performance.
[*] Doors in House now automatically close over time, in order to allow for occlusion portal functionality, providing a significant increase in performance.
[*] Introduced more aggressive LOD-culling in certain house locations to reduce known framerate spikes.
[*] Improved physics solver iterations for more performant and stable physics.
[*] Widespread improvements to object LODs.
[*] Improvements to character models that reduce the number of active skinned meshes in a scene, improving performance.
[*] Modified character visemes for more natural and performant facial animation.
[*] Improved keyframe animation compression.
[*] Some alpha textures are converted to mesh in order to improve performance.
[*] Dropping the task letter will no longer result in framerate spikes.
[*] Fixed a memory leak with line renderers.
[*] Some transparent shaders were replaced with additive transparency, improving performance in key locations.
[*] Fixed some lighting artefacts, and rebaked lighting + occlusion to be more performant.
[*] Audience members are now less demanding on performance. 
[*] Updated and improved backend toolsets and SDKs to improve runtime performance.
[*] Loads of small scale performance improvements across the whole game.
[/list]

[h3]General Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] Adjusted colliders of all “container” objects across the game to make carrying things more accurate and performant.
[*] Rattling drawers will no longer cause their contents to explode.
[*] Updated player body collisions to no longer collide with grabbable or dynamic objects unless necessary to a task. This should improve manipulation of large objects.
[*] Minor modifications to throwing objects.
[*] Performance improvements when using polaroid camera
[*] Can no longer skip past important “trigger zones” using the teleport movement when Backstage.
[*] Switching hands while a task card is opening will no longer cause the opening animation to pause.
[*] Breakable objects will no longer destroy other breakable objects they are touching.
[*] Anything with a hinge joint will now behave itself.
[*] Kitchen layout has been adjusted slightly.
[*] Video instructions in backstage tutorial made clearer.
[*] A large number of minor updates to scoring and task clarity.
[*] Alex blows his whistle at the end of tasks more consistently.
[/list]

notes.content:

Step into the contestants’ shoes by competing in extraordinary challenges or fill the industrious boots of the Taskmaster’s Assistant by creating tasks of your own!

As a contestant, you'll complete a series of amusing and bemusing challenges with the aspiration of becoming Taskmaster champion - these tasks are puzzling, physical and designed to allow for outside-the-box thinking with multiple solutions!

notes.title: Announcing Taskmaster VR: Creative Mode!
notes.content:
[h1]Announcing Taskmaster VR: Creative Mode![/h1]

[previewyoutube=K-ZF7K9RuaE;full][/previewyoutube]

Aspiring assistants take note - we’ve just announced that [b] Creative Mode is coming to Taskmaster VR! [/b]

Your journey into the world of Taskmaster doesn’t end when you lift that glittering golden bonce in triumph - Creative Mode lets you slip into Alex and Greg’s shiny shoes and create your own tasks! Wielding hundreds of oddball objects and an arsenal of useful tools, you can get creative and let your inner Alex shine - perfect for challenging your friends in local play.

[h2]What is Creative Mode?[/h2]
Creative Mode is a custom sandbox feature that we’ve developed for TMVR that allows players to design and set their own challenging and extraordinary tasks. You are given the run of the Taskmaster House, as well as access to a number of useful tools and toys that can be set up in almost any configuration of game objects that you like. Then, all you need to do is set up the starting position, save and pass it to a friend to make a fool of themselves with!

[h3]Key Features[/h3]

[list]
[*] Create your own tasks and challenge your friends in local play!
[*] Hundreds of unique items, furniture and fruit to play with.
[*] Save and share in local play - perfect for Taskmaster parties.
[*] Making tasks isn’t compulsory - Creative Mode is also great for exploring the taskmaster house, coming up with new task strategies, or just making a big mess.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/9d861f1829117d2e8c2d7778417045a7fc176261.png[/img]

[h2]What Inspired the Development of Creative Mode?[/h2]
Taskmaster VR is a labour of love for us, and we’ve always been very open about[url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD][b] listening to the community of the game[/b][/url] and the show, and what they want!

We saw the huge outpouring of requests for modding support, but we wanted to take things a step further and create something uniquely Taskmaster. The team have been so inspired by all the stories our discord community have shared with us about Taskmaster parties they’ve thrown for friends and family, as well as by amazing initiatives like [url=https://taskmaster.tv/hometasking][b]Home Tasking[/b][/url] during the difficult covid lockdowns and [url=https://taskmastereducation.com/school-tasking][b]School Tasking[/b][/url] - which is helping to bring the joy of Taskmaster to schools and colleges in the UK.

Creative Mode came naturally from there. We’ve built all these fun toys when designing our tasks, but why wouldn’t we let you play with them too? Sharing is caring, after all.

We asked the team behind the feature what they're most looking forward to.

[i]“I grew up playing creative games like minecraft, and I love that if you give a player the right tools, we can let our creativity run wild and make stuff you never imagined! I’m really excited to see what people make with this.” - Cory, Developer[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/6bb1d225c39e05694d140512fe1c0d7b9e3f63eb.png[/img]

[h2]Roadmap & Next Steps[/h2]
We can’t wait to see what you’ll build with Creative Mode, and we’re desperate to see your creations on launch day and beyond - but things won’t be stopping there.

Creative Mode 1.0 is an intentionally simple, minimalist feature - but it won’t always be that way. We have an exciting roadmap of updates that we’re excited to share with you over the coming weeks and months. We’re exploring new additions like enhanced sharing, more interactive objects and locations, crafting - and more, even more exciting things. It's still early days on these - some of them may not work out. Which is why we have a task for [i]you[/i], the community.

[b]What do you want to see? [/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD][b]Tell us how you would use this feature[/b][/url], what tasks you would like to create, and how best we can work together to build the #VRTasking community! (Catchy hashtag, right?) 


[h2]How Can I Find Out More?[/h2]
[url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD][b]Join the discord![/b][/url] This is the best place to chat directly with our developers and other Taskmaster fans about Taskmaster VR and our work on the game. You can also follow us on our social media, such as[url=https://twitter.com/scallywagarcade][b] twitter/x[/b][/url] or[url=https://www.instagram.com/scallywagarcade/][b] instagram![/b][/url]

notes.title: Accessibility Options in Taskmaster VR
notes.content:
Accessibility is a cornerstone of Scallywag Arcade’s approach to game design - it is important to us that our games can be played and enjoyed by as many people as possible, without ever making anyone feel as though they are getting a compromised play experience. This has been of particular importance when adapting Taskmaster for VR - a platform where individual accessibility and comfort needs can vary wildly between players in a way that might not happen with a traditional controller and screen!

We set out with the express goals of making Taskmaster playable no matter what your particular needs might be, or your home environment. All our tasks are benchmarked to be playable when seated and standing, as well as if you play stationary or at roomscale.

We also recognise that accessibility needs are a spectrum, and so we resolved to offer as many as we could to all players in as flexible a manner as possible. Let’s take a look at a list of some of the accessibility options you can use to tailor your Taskmaster experience…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/3e2b47532535c887df501e657d76d711dc989be5.png[/img]

[h3]Multiple Movement Options[/h3]
Whether you would prefer to move your own body, teleport around, or use a controller thumbstick for Continuous movement,  our Tasks will work with all three. Our teleport setup allows for fine tuning of direction, and additional customisation options for each movement mode are available - including snap vs smooth turning, dominant hand selection, and the choice to use your head or your controller to dictate continuous forward movement axis. However you prefer to move in VR, we’re hopeful that we’ll support you.

[h3]Height Management and Adjustment[/h3]
For seated play, we have a height calibration tool that will help ensure you are comfortable and able to reach those all-important watermelons Alex keeps leaving around the place. The tool is also available in standing mode, in case you want to make some small adjustments to your in-game height.

[h3]Dynamic Crouch Toggle[/h3]
A simple one, but a small one - not everyone is able to crawl around on their hands and knees trying not to knock over towers of tin cans, so we have implemented a button press crouch.

[h3]Force Grab[/h3]
Will we get sued for this one? Let’s find out! If you’re finding that grabbing the things you need from certain heights or angles is difficult, players can increase the distance that they can grab interactive items by selecting their target and pulling it towards them. Some of the contestants could have used this on the show…

[h3]Colour Vision Deficiency Support By Design[/h3]
Our Tasks (and the game as a whole) have, wherever possible, taken into account various CVD conditions to ensure that your experience is minimally impacted without the need for specific filters or vision modes. The game uses a colour palette specifically chosen to help support this! There are certain popular Taskmaster items or set dressings that we have chosen to make small changes to as well - the Red Green, for example, is referred to as a “Red Circle” in Taskmaster VR - as we found in accessibility testing it was not clear to CVD users what item we were talking about, or that it got lost when placed on the grass in the garden. You can see this visual language throughout the game, where use of colour is supported with shapes, patterns and symbols to aid baseline readability.

[h3]Vignettes and Tunnelling[/h3]
Tunnelling is a technique where a vignette is used to reduce the player’s visibility when making particularly fast movements like turning or teleporting, as an anti-sickness measure. In a physics based game like Taskmaster where the player has a real presence in the world, this becomes even more important. Tunnelling in Taskmaster VR is activated on a feature by feature basis, and also offers an intensity slider so that you can tailor it for your specific needs!

[h3]Grip Toggle[/h3]
Another simple one, but powerful - you spend a lot of time grabbing stuff and waggling it around in Taskmaster. This setting allows you to either press and hold the Grip button to hold an item, releasing it to let go - or to use a single button press to “toggle” the state of an object from grab to release. This setting is mostly useful for anyone with any kind of motor challenges or chronic pain. 

[h3]Menu Distances[/h3]
A floating menu can often be a hard thing to get right, so we ... allow you to adjust the distance at which it's displayed from your face. We’re also working on allowing you to adjust the size and scale too!

[h3]Audio and Subtitle Controls[/h3]
You can adjust and mute various aspects of the game individually - music, sound effects and dialogue. In addition, the game offers subtitles designed for readability and clarity - there are visual indicators of who is speaking, and the direction from which the speech is coming from!

[h3]Arachnophobia Mode[/h3]
This one was actually really easy for us to implement, as there are no spiders in the game at all. You’re welcome, world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/78407bad82c6b580efe6d5057eaee62b5a966d02.png[/img]

[h2]Accessibility By Design[/h2]
Why is accessibility so important to us? Firstly, we’re a diverse studio with a team from all walks of life, and we’re making the games that we’d like to see, without compromising the silliness and chaos of Taskmaster. As a studio, we work with a number of charities to champion awareness of Accessibility By Design, and to help share the incredible world of videogames without barriers - we’re patrons of both Special Effect and Safe In Our World - and we regularly invite them to our studio to check out all our fun toys, and to give us advice and guidance on how to build better games.

We’re always looking for new ways to improve our accessibility offerings in game, so we’d love to hear from the community what we can do to help you with mastering these tasks. Hit us up in the comments or on Discord!

notes.title: Meet the Characters - Little Alex Horne
notes.content:
It’s time to introduce a man with the fashion sense and personality of a sausage that rolled under the fridge six weeks ago! He’s the Taskmaster’s assistant, personal trainer and - when necessary - therapy animal…it’s Little Alex Horne! A familiar face to fans of the show, Alex is ever present at your side as a (mostly) neutral observer. He’s passive, unflappable and pretty much up for absolutely anything that will please his boss. Alex is a much less bombastic character than that of the Taskmaster, and this is reflected in the design of his video game counterpart!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/978901189da2b7eb460be7cfbe11de41679453c4.png[/img]

Alex is a constant presence in the game and the show, and so capturing and exaggerating his mannerisms, voice and general vibe was just as critical as it was for the Taskmaster himself. Alex has provided face capture, voice acting and mocap reference for his VR doppelganger, and will always be there for you with an incredibly helpful observation on just how poorly you are performing.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/169ea164bebb0f47dc081ee6dd9bf2c6bc36c46f.png[/img]

Stylistically, Alex and Greg need to complement each other - where Greg is an all-encompassing presence and form, Alex needed to be the opposite. You spend much more time with Alex than Greg - he needs to be a subtler entity, a companion and observer but not one that steals your attention and gets in your space the way Greg does. We’ve taken some artistic liberties to achieve this - going through a number of iterations in design to find our perfect interpretation of Alex!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/97f5ba3fce4564b701599a857c100932fe63a30c.png[/img]

Alex’s diminutive stature and submissive nature are brought out in his spindly legs, for example, and his real-world height (a fairly massive 6’ 2”!) has been reduced to something more in line with the show’s narrative. We also increased Greg’s height (to 7’ 7”, fact fans) to emphasise this further!

Just like on the telly, Alex was keen for us to parody and caricature some of his more distinctive features, including his hair, eyes and teeth - and these have been designed in a way to allow us some pretty expressive looks, while still staying true to the technological limitations and facial animation features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/dc34e133bb8688d86b2fbb905de447a429975a3b.png[/img]

The clipboard, the stopwatch, the wry looks and the witty comments - The Taskmaster’s Assistant wants you to succeed and will be an ever-present part of your TMVR experience.

notes.title: Meet the Characters - The Taskmaster
notes.content:
[h1]Meet the Taskmaster![/h1]
He’s mighty, he’s tall, and he’s dressed to impress - meet The Taskmaster! The titular titan is played by legendary comedian Greg Davies in both the TV show and Taskmaster VR, but how did we approach bringing his familiar face, voice and general gravitas into the virtual world?

First - a quick 101 on the role of The Taskmaster. The Taskmaster is the arbiter of your efforts to complete tasks and will reward you with points based on both the success of your attempts and…well, his own subjective whims and fancies. Think of him as the king and you as the court jester! Questioning his approach or the scoreboard won’t get you very far - that’s why he has an assistant for you to query and poke at with justifications for your unhinged actions instead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/e08f05ae81e4b1a1a9fdf90de93d5283796c885f.png[/img]

Any fan of the show will know Greg Davies, beloved in the global comedy circuit for his no nonsense personality. He’s tall in stature and confident in voice, something we wanted to ensure came across in the game. VR is great for realising scale - most contestants will find that Greg is imposing enough while just sitting on his throne, let alone when standing up - and we wanted to ensure that we reflected (and slightly exaggerated) this!

Initially, our focus was on identifying who The Taskmaster truly is. Rather than honing in on Greg Davies the actor, we took inspiration from the persona he embodies in the Taskmaster TV show. We meticulously studied his appearance, personality and mannerisms - helped out in no small part by our voiceover and facial capture sessions, which gave us the opportunity to get up close and personal with the man himself! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/307d3325867b1c4e056944375d1c01700863d186.png[/img]

We designed his height, shape, and overall silhouette to evoke a sense of intimidation and awe - but we also wanted to make sure that there's a slightly heroic edge to him! The Taskmaster is fully capable of benevolence after all - he isn’t the villain! Greg is slightly taller in Taskmaster VR than in real life - and its a lot of fun to stand on stage and have him towering over you!

At every stage of development, if was important to keep the design of Alex Horne in mind as well - they needed to complement each other. After all, they’re like a comedy Batman and Robin - contrasting characters that nevertheless feel like two parts of a whole.

One of the most important parts of Taskmaster is interacting with the hosts - you spend a lot of time up close and personal with them, so we needed to make sure that their facial expressions, animations and body language were as immersive as the hardware restrictions would allow! Greg’s thoughts and presence are often communicated through looks alone, so it was crucial to get this right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/a27de1bd275e0b2c954f2728fe8d232ca0481cb6.png[/img]

We created loads of sculpted iterations of Greg's face, exploring how best to strike a balance between our bright, stylised aesthetic, capturing his character and providing the technical wotsits required for facial animation. Once we found the desired balance, we further refined it by determining which features to enhance or soften, including considerations like ageing and typical facial expressions reflecting his mood. We decided to emphasise the character's constant air of contempt towards contestants - the game is set in the fictional world of Taskmaster remember - while allowing for moments of elation, amusement, or anger. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/ecd20bb60ffa6549188bdb3aefd231c4f2b7996c.png[/img]

Finally, once we had our character models in a good place, we consulted with Greg and Alex themselves! After workshopping, we ended up leaning more towards their current appearances than their depictions in earlier seasons - however, we did maintain a slight contrast by not making Alex's hair quite as grey as requested, in order to ensure a visual distinction from Greg!

Think you’re ready to impress? Take on his challenges (and some of Alex’s too) and task your heart out to win the best prize of all - a gold(ish) trophy modelled after his very own face.

notes.title: Exploring the Taskmaster House: The Caravan
notes.content:
Out in the garden, nestled amongst white picket fences, is where you’ll find the Taskmaster Caravan - a mundane staple of the British Staycation that has nevertheless been the staging ground of some truly extraordinary goings-on. Almost as well-known as the famous faces who pass through it, the caravan is hands-down the cutest space in the house - assuming you find the faint smell of mildew “cute” - and is a firm fan favourite. There was absolutely no way we were leaving it out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/2659151f5db96621d3be8a4854b08ccd4162d827.png[/img]

In Taskmaster VR, however, the caravan presented us with a problem that wasn’t immediately apparent during our research trips to the House - caravans are small, tightly enclosed spaces, and this one in particular is filled with a lot of stuff. Given the field of view and spacial perception available on most VR headsets, we found that we had to limit player time in this space to avoid overwhelming feelings of claustrophobia, discomfort and ennui. This means that while our tasks make use of the caravan, you won’t be required to spend long periods of gameplay in a space that goes against our core accessibility pillars. More on those in the coming weeks!

This doesn’t mean that fans of the show won’t get to explore this iconic location however! The Caravan is one of the most detailed locations we’ve built, and is full of all kinds of cool things - from family photos of Greg and Alex, to alluring stuffed animals, to the ever-popular crochet puppets you met in [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6NwH2dUBHEw]our reveal trailer. [/url][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/8a6ba2b5e50f45ccd6f67ed32c8ef5b5c4a796cf.png[/img]

The caravan is a lovely respite from the mess and stress of the house itself, giving players the opportunity to spend time in an entirely different stressful mess. It’s colourful, inviting and we can’t wait for you to explore it - just don’t bump your head on the way in, Alex hasn’t bothered to insure it for years.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/e250104861dc695144ab4609ba7cb960f9bd37fe.gif[/img]

Learn more about all the locations in [b][url=https://discord.com/channels/1130452265770160128/1130456942410739722/1172483283804770334]Taskmaster VR on our Discord![/url][/b]

notes.title: Exploring the Taskmaster House: The Lab
notes.content:
What does your dream house look like? A big cinema room? Perhaps it has a pool? Or a croquet lawn, that would be nice. What about a lab space? We’re talking a stark, wipe-clean area that has an air of veterinary surgery about it. For The Taskmaster and his overworked assistant it is an essential - after all, tasking is often a filthy undertaking. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/2484054f14e01d87e9843b90b727b166f2a8bd08.png[/img]

The Lab isn’t quite like other laboratories, although its premise is somewhat similar - experiment with interesting stuff and get messy. Expect to find the apparatus you need to complete the task at hand and four plastic sheeting-lined walls,where pretty much anything goes. In contrast to last week where we headed outside to show you the luscious green garden and its luscious green lawn, this is a more functional space and one that is only as colourful as the mess you make in there!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/5da7cd88a5d472a39f8d72fb955f68e416f62e0b.png[/img]

When reimagining the Taskmaster House for VR, sometimes we had to make small changes to make it work with gameplay - this hasn’t been the case with the Lab. It's a surprisingly roomy, completely empty space perfect for helping players focus on the important parts of the task, and we’ve kept everything except the slight smell of rotten milk that still permeates the air. Of course - just because a task starts in the lab, it doesn’t always mean you have to stay in there! Taskmaster is about thinking outside the box, and unless the task specifically prevents certain actions there is nothing stopping you going outside and grabbing the wheelie bin for whatever nefarious purposes you see fit!

notes.title: Exploring the Taskmaster House - The Garden
notes.content:
Like a contented Dad, last week we spent the day in the shed. Today we’ll be opening the doors and stepping out into the sunshine in [b]the Taskmaster Garden![/b]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/9ec3b9b19cbda5d9db007441e77a43f77432d2a6.png[/img]

The garden is central to the Taskmaster experience. It’s a versatile space that connects just about every  area of the game together. It’s verdant, secluded and liberally peppered with objet d’art, tools and what can only be described as ‘bits and bobs’. In Taskmaster VR, The Garden is used for Tasks that need a bit more space than the various rooms of the house might normally provide - or for when more large scale creativity is the name of the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/8cad25af546cd369b5c8a260e4f30991679a3287.png[/img]

As part of our very important research we sent the Scallywag Arcade away team to both the Taskmaster House and the studio. While exploring the house we found it to be the ideal space for tackling tasks, although like all good movie stars, it’s smaller than you expect in person. For those tasks that require space, stepping out in the garden we found ample room for all kinds of frolics. Our aim is to give players of Taskmaster VR a feel for what a bright, enticing space this is and how ideal it is for tomfoolery and tasks that simply can't be confined by four walls. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/c66bb6a3222d6ec90c4eb9b88aec9fe61b6f88c7.png[/img]

If you are a Taskmaster sage you can expect to find all your show favourites out in the garden - from the bathtub and phonebox to the stage and its door to nowhere - as well as old friends like Ollie the Knight, Greg’s statue and a lifesize model milking cow named Linda. Did you know that Linda has working mechanical udders that are used for practicing milking? Or that she was formally named by Taskmaster alumni Rylan Clark after his mum?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/6df127e9916fe429c30ea73d846c1fe4731afddc.png[/img]

Even if the virtual version is the first you have seen of the garden we think you’ll feel right at home indulging in a little mayhem amongst its menagerie of colourful characters.

notes.title: Exploring The Taskmaster House - The Shed
notes.content:
[h3]Time for a Tour![/h3]

You’ll be spending a lot of time in the [b]Taskmaster House[/b], hidden away in a secret location somewhere in the little district of Chiswick in the UK - so why not get acquainted with your new home away from home before getting started on some VR tasking?

Though some tasks may restrict your available locations, you will more often than not have [b]the run of the place[/b]. This means you'll get unfettered access to a decade’s worth of junk, odds and ends, bric-a-brac and - occasionally - [b]useful tools and resources[/b] that will aid you in completing even the most fiendish of tasks. Need something sharp? Off you pop to the kitchen to rifle through the cutlery drawer! Looking for the perfect sized plank of wood? Perhaps the garage will have what you need!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/ddba9e405781bd31c59f8611a4d68be3e8ca3c6a.png[/img]

Today, however, we’re looking at one of the most useful locations in the house that the more outdoorsy and dad-vibe types amongst you will find particularly appealing- The Shed!

For any soul brave enough to take on the piles of dusty cardboard boxes and the somewhat distressing smell, you’ll find all kinds of treasures in the shed - from sports equipment and balls of different sizes, to litter-picker-uppers and handheld vacuum cleaners. There’s even a little pile of almost-real rubber bricks, should they take your fancy - I’m sure they’ll be useful [i]somehow[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/61452ffa6961d0a8b24a840f6d768874f1ad6d46.png[/img]
[h3]Shed-loads of stuff![/h3]

The shed contains a mix of items that are permanent - they’ll always be there for you - and on occasion, some [b]task-specific switch ups[/b]. A key part of the game is thinking outside the box - remember, there is never a single solution to a task. What matters is YOUR solution, and the Taskmaster House is here to help facilitate that - so matter what you might need, the shed is a great place to start looking for it.

What would you like to see in the Shed? Is there a particular location you'd like to see more of? [url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD][b]Join hundreds of other TM fans on Discord[/b][/url] and let us know!

notes.title: California Dreamin' - The Taskmaster House in VR
notes.content:
Every season of Taskmaster has a [b]theme [/b]- a whimsical redecorating of the house to reflect the current mood and fancies of the Taskmaster. From Salvador Dali and Andy Warhol to Steampunk, vegetables and the Wild West, the Taskmaster house has been redecorated more times than Alex has been allowed hot dinners - and your house in Taskmaster VR is no different.

Greg, Alex and the rest of the Taskmaster team have been gracious enough to allow us to design our own theme for TMVR, and we think it's a doozy. [b]Greg’s been craving a little bit of sunshine recently[/b], so we redecorated and gave him…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/29da4f3b0784657d7c0d2c3ae1fbe03c72865294.png[/img]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/9e7468bc0a6307c9de16047e02b0e4ac72326511.png[/img]

Endless summers, coastal adventures, and chill sunshine pop on the radio - welcome to California Tasking! Expect to see a symphony of pastel pinks and azure blues, subtle touches of warm gold and...plastic lawn flamingos - Alex has to stick to a budget after all! 

We went through a [i]lot [/i]of different theme ideas, but in the end we wanted one that reflected both our overall aesthetic direction, and that would support our core message - that the Taskmaster house is [b]welcoming and full of life![/b] You’ll be spending a lot of time here, and we want it to feel like home - even if some of the tasks may occasionally have you questioning that!

Designing a theme for the Taskmaster house has been a dream come true for all of us at Scallywag Arcade, and we’re so, so proud to have contributed to the world and story of Taskmaster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/780ed68f611dd52fbad29e305631409e898a275e.png[/img]

One final thing…what would the Taskmaster House be without a beautiful, bespoke portrait of the Taskmaster? Drawing influence from the vibrant works of Matisse and Rousseau, our Taskmaster portrait embraces the spirit of vintage travel posters and incorporates the vibrant hues of Miami Vice - and we thought you might like to have one too!

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3114474307]Head over the Taskmaster VR Community Page[/url] to download a gorgeous mobile wallpaper, so you can take Greg with you wherever you go. Don’t forget to thank him!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/3d2d44a3e245ee21cac34de6190f31c80ace8fba.png[/img]

Do you have a dream house theme you’d love to see on Taskmaster? What is your favourite house theme from the show? [url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD]Join hundreds of other TM fans on Discord[/url] and let’s chat!

notes.title: What is Taskmaster VR?
notes.content:
If you are an avid (or even rabid) fan of Taskmaster then you’ll already know what you’re getting into - however, if you're new to this global comedy phenomenon then we’re here to [b]walk you through it![/b]

Taskmaster is an offbeat comedy game show created in the UK but popular with millions of fans all around the world. The premise is simple - you will be given a cornucopia of[b] challenging and extraordinary tasks[/b] and charged with their completion by [b]any means you see fit![/b] Your efforts will then be judged by The Taskmaster, earning you sweet, delicious - and completely arbitrary - [b]points.[/b] Yum yum yum.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/78407bad82c6b580efe6d5057eaee62b5a966d02.png[/img]


Let’s start with The Taskmaster and his assistant. [b]Legendary comedian Greg Davies[/b] is the titular Taskmaster - and what a mighty sight he is. A towering giant of a man, yet one who spends most of the show lounging on his golden throne. Greg is witty, unruffled and incredibly self assured - all ideal for [b]passing judgement on whatever clever little loopholes[/b] you think you may have found.

His subservient assistant Little Alex Horne is the true brains behind the operation. Alex is the show’s creator and is the one who will dish out the tasks, as well as your [b]ever-present guide and invigilator through the house and beyond.[/b] He’s always ready with a helpful comment reminding you of the rules, or to pedantically point out [b]each and every mistake[/b] you make. A class act. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/3e2b47532535c887df501e657d76d711dc989be5.png[/img]


You’ll be doing most of your tasking in either the Taskmaster studio or the iconic Taskmaster House in the exotic borough of Chiswick, UK. [b]Every task starts with a wax sealed letter[/b] - just open it up, read through your objectives, and begin as soon as the timer starts. Previous contestants have been tasked with finding hidden pineapples, hurling toilet rolls around an airport - or even running their own hotel for an afternoon - and with all Taskmaster VR’s tasks being [b]designed exclusively for the game[/b], you’ll need to expect the unexpected and be ready for anything.

Your job is to complete the task - however you see fit - within the constraints that Alex will place on you, and there is [b]rarely a single correct way to do so[/b]! Use lateral thinking - and an entire house filled to the brim with all kinds of useful tat - to express yourself and complete the task [i]your way.[/i]

Once the task is complete, judgement - and a score - is given by The Taskmaster. Expect laughs, questionably-constructive feedback - and for the truly outstanding, even a dash of admiration. He’s not a monster.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44769901/ad5626a98dd331999ba033754918d10bb60b8827.png[/img]


Tasks are grouped into episodes and the episodes form a series - which means we get a series champion who takes home a [b]spectacular trophy[/b] modelled on Greg’s head. Imagine having that bad boy on your coffee table. And it being virtual means you don’t need to polish it every Sunday. Fantastic news.

It really is as simple as that! We’re so excited with the amazing response to Taskmaster VR, and we cannot wait for you to join us and show the world what you can do. Join [url=https://discord.gg/mHGM3SsRjD]hundreds of other Taskmaster fans on discord[/url], or jump into the comments, and tell us what you’d like to see next!

Your time starts now!
